items.purpose: The service catalogue entry tells consumers and the service desk exactly what the Beacon patient-flow analytics service is, who it is for, what it does (utility), how well it is assured (warranty), how it is supported and which service levels Kestrel commits to. The Programme Manager drafts it with Grace Liu (E-005), the service owner. Janelle Cardinal (E-008), business owner of the Power BI service (A-009), and Marcus Bell (E-002) approve it. You write version 1.0 in week 4, before the reports exist, so the service levels shape the design. It is used at go-live, by the service desk when it triages a ticket, and at every service review. In week 6 you add the record of the first service review.

sections.heading: Service summary
sections.guidance: Give the service a name and ID, a one-sentence description in the consumer's language, the consumer groups, the business owner and service owner, the classification and how someone gets access. It is good when a charge nurse can tell in thirty seconds whether this is the service they need and how to get it.

sections.heading: Utility: what the service does
sections.guidance: Utility is fit for purpose. State the outcome consumers want, then list what the service does as the questions it answers and the measure that answers each one. Add what the service does not do, so nobody expects it. Good utility traces every feature to a consumer outcome, not to a count of visuals.

sections.heading: Warranty: how well it is assured
sections.guidance: Warranty is fit for use. Cover availability, capacity and performance, security and continuity, each with a concrete commitment and its source (an agreed service level, a test plan or the asset register). A warranty line with no number or no owner is a wish, so rewrite it until someone could test it.

sections.heading: Support model
sections.guidance: Show who handles what at each support level, how tickets are routed in the IT Service Management Platform (A-011), when to escalate, and which internal agreements and supplier contracts the service depends on. Name the support risks, such as one key person or a contract that ends soon. It is good when the service desk could route any ticket without asking the project team.

sections.heading: Service levels
sections.guidance: List five to eight measures consumers care about. For each give the target, label it agreed or proposed, give the baseline from data and say where it is measured. Use Kestrel's existing priority targets rather than inventing new ones. Every target needs a measurement source before go-live, or the first review cannot judge it.

sections.heading: First service review (week 6)
sections.guidance: Record the date, chair, attendees and period, then what the review found for service levels, consumer feedback, risks and data quality, with the action and owner for each. Be honest about what is too early to judge: a monthly target cannot be judged on three days. Every action should point to a continual-improvement register item or a change request.

sections.heading: Approval and review cadence
sections.guidance: Say who approved which version and when, how often service reviews happen and who chairs them, and how a service level is changed. A change that alters scope, cost or data handling goes through the change-control board, not only the service review.

| Document ID | BCN-R1-23 |
| Title | Service catalogue entry and service levels: Beacon Patient-Flow Analytics |
| Service owner | Grace Liu (E-005), IT Service Desk Manager |
| Business owner | Janelle Cardinal (E-008), Director of Patient Flow |
| Approvers | Janelle Cardinal (E-008); Marcus Bell (E-002), Chief Information Officer |
| Version and date | 1.1, 2026-10-28 (1.0 approved 2026-10-02) |
| Status | Approved; first service review recorded |

## Service summary

- Service: Beacon Patient-Flow Analytics (SVC-BCN-01), delivered through the Power BI service and Beacon semantic model (A-009).
- Description: daily, de-identified dashboards of emergency department (ED) waits and bed pressure for each of Kestrel's four sites. It replaces the Excel extracts emailed every morning.
- Consumers: executives, patient-flow leaders, ED leaders and charge nurses at each site, clinical analysts.
- Classification: Confidential. On every app page, counts under 5 are suppressed, along with any total that would reveal them by subtraction, and any rate whose numerator is under 5 is blank (Kestrel reporting rule).
- Access: an access request through the service desk. Your site role decides which rows you see (row-level security, RLS).

## Utility: what the service does

Outcome: one trusted set of numbers each morning, so leaders act on waits and beds instead of arguing about whose extract is right.

| Question answered | Measure (Kestrel definition) |
|---|---|
| How long do patients wait to be seen? | Median minutes from arrival to physician initial assessment (PIA); % PIA within Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale (CTAS) target |
| How many leave before being seen? | Left without being seen (LWBS) rate |
| How long do patients stay in the ED? | Median ED length of stay (LOS), admitted and discharged |
| How full are our beds? | Occupancy, average daily and last snapshot; alternate level of care (ALC) patient-days |

Not provided: patient-level lists. Care teams use the Clinical Information System (CIS, A-001) for patient detail.

## Warranty: how well it is assured

| Area | Commitment | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Availability | Viewable at all hours; scheduled refresh daily at 05:00 Mountain Time, so dashboards show yesterday's data by 06:00; a refresh failure alerts the service desk (Analytics Support) within 1 hour | Service level (agreed) |
| Capacity and performance | Every visual renders in 3 seconds or less in Performance Analyzer | Report specification (agreed) |
| Security | RLS by site, Confidential sensitivity label, app-only access, quarterly access review | Security acceptance criteria |
| Continuity | Recovery time objective 72 hours, recovery point objective 24 hours for A-009 | Asset register (data) |

## Support model

| Level | Who | Handles |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Service desk (Grace Liu, E-005, service owner) | Logs every contact in the IT Service Management Platform (A-011) under category Power BI, answers how-to questions from knowledge articles, sends access requests to Identity and Access |
| 2 | Analytics Support (Mei Tanaka, E-013) | Refresh failures, wrong-number reports, report defects |
| 3 | Tomás Rivera (E-006), data steward | Model and measure fixes, RLS, releases |
| Supplier | Lumen Analytics Partners (V-05), fixed price to 2026-11-30 | Defects in the Release 1 build |

- Priority 1 and 2 (P1, P2) incidents go straight to level 3; Janelle Cardinal hears of any P1.
- Operational level agreements: Clinical Analytics for model fixes; Infrastructure (Ahmed Haddad, E-017) for the on-premises data gateway.
- Support risks: one model builder (R-06); Lumen leaves 2026-11-30 (R-07).

## Service levels

Agreed by Janelle Cardinal (business owner) and Grace Liu (service owner) on 2026-10-02 and judged monthly. Baselines: khn_service_desk.csv, 27 tickets in the Power BI category, August and September 2026.

| Service level | Target | Baseline (data) | Measured in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yesterday's data showing by 06:00 | 95% of days (agreed) | None: extracts were manual | Refresh history |
| Incidents resolved within priority target (P1 4 h, P2 8 h, P3 24 h, P4 72 h) | 90% (agreed) | 66.7% (8 of 12), median 12.0 h | A-011 |
| Service requests within target | 85% (agreed) | 50.0% (4 of 8), median 48.3 h | A-011 |
| Access to the app within 72 hours | 80% (agreed, charter) | 1 of 6, median 4.40 days | A-011 |
| Measures match the reconciliation figures | 100% of release checks (agreed) | Every catalogue measure matched at user acceptance testing | Quality plan test log |
| No count under 5 and no cross-site rows | Zero failures (agreed) | Go-live condition D-02 | RLS test pack |
| Satisfaction on Power BI tickets | 4.0 of 5 (proposed) | 3.0 from 9 responses | Closure survey |

## First service review (week 6)

- Date: 2026-10-28, in the first week of early life support. Chair: Grace Liu, service owner. Present: Janelle Cardinal, Tomás Rivera, Mei Tanaka, Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007), Programme Manager.
- Period: 2026-10-26 (app opened) to 2026-10-28. Too short to judge monthly targets; the first full month is judged at review 2.

| Topic | Finding | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Measurement | Refresh history, the Power BI category and the closure survey are all capturing data | None |
| Baseline gaps | Access to the app (1 of 6 within 72 hours) is the widest gap, then requests (50.0%) and incidents (66.7%) | CI-01, CI-02; CI-03 waits |
| Consumer feedback | Janelle Cardinal asked for a list of ALC patients by name and bed number on the bed page | Logged as CR-01 for the change-control board on 2026-10-29, which must weigh the Health Information Act duties: least amount of information, highest degree of anonymity |
| Risks | R-06 and R-07 threaten level 3 support | CI-05 |
| Satisfaction | Few survey responses (9 in the baseline) | CI-07 |

Decision: targets unchanged. Review 2: 2026-11-25.

## Approval and review cadence

- Version 1.0 approved 2026-10-02 by Janelle Cardinal and Marcus Bell. Version 1.1 adds the review record.
- Monthly service review chaired by the service owner, Grace Liu, with the business owner, Janelle Cardinal: service levels, tickets, feedback, risks and the continual-improvement register.
- Service levels change only when both approvers agree at a review. A change to scope, cost or data handling goes to the change-control board.
mistakes: Writing utility as a feature list (pages and visuals) instead of the outcomes consumers need and the questions the service answers.
Setting service levels with no baseline and no measurement source, so nobody can tell at the first review whether a target was met.
Leaving warranty vague: no recovery objective, no security controls and no performance target, so a correct dashboard can still fail its users when it matters.
Judging monthly targets on a few days of data, or ending the review with no owned, dated actions in the continual-improvement register.

items.purpose: This is the report specification for the Beacon app. It defines every page before and while it is built: who each page is for, the questions it answers, its visuals and measures, the value each measure must show when tested, how small counts are suppressed, how users move between pages, and the accessibility and performance tests. The Programme Manager writes it with Janelle Cardinal (E-008) and Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007), who approve it. Tomás Rivera (E-006) builds from it, testers use it in user acceptance testing, and the service desk uses it to answer 'is this number right?'. Version 1.0 comes from week 5 day 1 (pages and visuals); version 1.1 from day 2 (drillthrough, tooltips and bookmarks).

sections.heading: Audiences and questions
sections.guidance: Name each audience, give real people as examples, and write the questions they ask in their own words. Then say which page answers them. It is good when every page traces to at least one audience question and no audience is left without a page.

sections.heading: Page design
sections.guidance: Describe each page: its purpose, the visuals in reading order, the measure behind each visual and any reference lines or targets. Include hidden pages such as drillthrough and tooltip pages. Keep each page small enough to read in under a minute; if a page needs a scroll bar, split it.

sections.heading: Measures and tested values
sections.guidance: List every measure used, with the value it must show with no filter and for each site, taken from the approved reconciliation figures. These are the numbers testers compare against. A specification without expected values cannot be accepted, because nobody can say a number is wrong.

sections.heading: Small-count suppression
sections.guidance: State the Kestrel rule, where it applies, how counts, rates and medians behave below 5, and the test cases that prove it. Include the DAX pattern so the builder applies it the same way everywhere. Good suppression also blocks working a small count back from a rate and its total, or from a total minus the visible cells.

sections.heading: Navigation: drillthrough, tooltips and bookmarks
sections.guidance: Describe drillthrough (source visuals, target page, filters kept, back button), tooltip pages, bookmarks and what each one captures, page navigation, synced slicers and visual interactions. Check that navigation still respects row-level security. Good navigation lets a user go from 'which site?' to 'which triage level, when?' in two clicks.

sections.heading: Accessibility and performance
sections.guidance: List the checks every page must pass: alt text, tab order, contrast, meaning not carried by colour alone, readable font sizes, 'Show as a table', mobile layout and Performance Analyzer timings. Each check should be testable with a yes or no, and each target should say whether it is agreed or proposed.

sections.heading: Approval and change log
sections.guidance: Record each version with its date, what changed and who approved it, and say how changes are controlled after go-live. This proves the reports that went live are the ones the business owners approved.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document ID | BCN-R1-24 |
| Title | Executive and site operations reports: report specification |
| Owner | Programme Manager; builder Tomás Rivera (E-006) |
| Approvers | Janelle Cardinal (E-008); Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007) |
| Version and date | 1.1, 2026-10-16 |
| Status | Approved for build and user acceptance testing |

## Audiences and questions

| Audience | Example people | Their questions | Pages |
|---|---|---|---|
| Executives | Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001), Marcus Bell (E-002) | Are waits improving? Which site needs help? | Executive overview |
| Patient flow | Janelle Cardinal (E-008) | Where are beds tight? Where do ALC patients wait? | Executive overview, Beds and flow |
| Site ED leaders and charge nurses | Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007), Aisha Mahmoud (E-010), Dr. Liam O'Connor (E-012) | Which triage levels wait longest at my site, and when? | Site ED operations, Site detail |

Sites: Kestrel General Hospital (KGH), Aspen Ridge Hospital (ARH), Coulee Valley Hospital (CVH), Prairie Gate Health Centre (PGH). ED means emergency department.

## Page design

1. Executive overview: cards for median minutes to physician initial assessment (PIA), % PIA within Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale (CTAS) target, left without being seen (LWBS) rate and occupancy; bar chart of median minutes by site with a reference line at the KGH target of 60 minutes (agreed); weekly trend line; occupancy by site; matrix of admitted visits by site with a total, using ED Visits (Shared Total).
2. Site ED operations: CTAS table (visits, % within target, median minutes); length of stay (LOS) admitted versus discharged; arrivals by hour and weekday; LWBS rate by week.
3. Beds and flow: occupancy by unit; last snapshot cards; alternate level of care (ALC) patient-days by site.
4. Site detail: hidden drillthrough page.
5. Site tooltip: hidden tooltip page.
6. Definitions and data notes: Kestrel definitions, as-at date, last refresh, suppression rule.

At most 8 visuals a page (proposed). Date slicer synced on pages 1 to 3.

## Measures and tested values

Unsuppressed values, 2026-07-01 to 2026-09-30, from the approved reconciliation figures. Test in Power BI Desktop with no filter and with each site.

| Measure | All | KGH | ARH | CVH | PGH |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ED Visits | 474 | 213 | 105 | 101 | 55 |
| Median Minutes to PIA | 64.0 | 80.5 | 54.5 | 54.0 | 45.5 |
| % PIA Within CTAS Target | 28.3% | 12.8% | 34.0% | 39.2% | 55.8% |
| LWBS Rate | 5.7% | 7.5% | 4.8% | 4.0% | 3.6% |
| Median ED LOS Hours Admitted | 11.96 | 15.14 | 9.45 | 8.58 | 8.33 |
| Median ED LOS Hours Discharged | 3.61 | 4.30 | 3.30 | 3.02 | 2.91 |
| Occupancy % (Average Daily) | 87.0% | 89.3% | 84.8% | 87.9% | 76.8% |
| Occupancy % (Last Snapshot) | 84.0% | 84.7% | 82.5% | 86.4% | 80.0% |
| ALC Days | 2,075 | 835 | 561 | 377 | 302 |

Also test: % within target by CTAS level 42.9%, 33.3%, 15.6%, 30.5%, 58.9% (levels 1 to 5); last snapshot 121 of 144 staffed beds; evening arrivals 34.0%.

## Small-count suppression

Every app page is shared beyond the care team, so the rule applies on every page (agreed with Priya Raman, E-003, for R-02). A count under 5 shows as "<5". A rate whose numerator is under 5 is blank, with a footnote, so a count cannot be worked back from a rate and its total. Medians are not suppressed by this rule. Totals and subtotals that would reveal a suppressed cell by subtraction are suppressed too (Kestrel policy): in the Executive overview matrix of admitted visits by site, PGH (4) shows "<5", but the total of 59 would give it away (59 minus KGH 31, ARH 15 and CVH 9 leaves 4). The matrix therefore uses ED Visits (Shared Total), which blanks a total across sites whenever any site in the filter has 1 to 4 visits. Shared pages do not use a matrix with a second grouping and subtotals, such as site by disposition, because a row subtotal can leak a cell the same way. Text measures go in tables, matrices and cards; charts use numeric measures that return blank. The measures are the ones in the DAX catalogue (BCN-R1-20).

```
ED Visits (Shared) =
VAR Visits = [ED Visits]
RETURN
    IF ( ISBLANK ( Visits ), BLANK (), IF ( Visits < 5, "<5", FORMAT ( Visits, "#,0" ) ) )

LWBS Rate (Shared) =
VAR LWBSVisits = CALCULATE ( [ED Visits], FactEDVisit[Disposition] = "LWBS" )
RETURN
    IF ( LWBSVisits < 5, BLANK (), [LWBS Rate] )

ED Visits (Shared Total) =
VAR SmallSites =
    COUNTROWS (
        FILTER ( VALUES ( DimSite[SiteCode] ), [ED Visits] >= 1 && [ED Visits] <= 4 )
    )
RETURN
    IF (
        ISINSCOPE ( DimSite[SiteCode] ),
        [ED Visits (Shared)],
        IF ( SmallSites > 0, BLANK (), [ED Visits (Shared)] )
    )
```

Tests in app view: PGH LWBS (2 visits) shows "<5" and its rate is blank; CVH LWBS (4) shows "<5" and its rate is blank; ARH LWBS (5) shows 5 and 4.8%; PGH admitted visits (4) show "<5", while the PGH median LOS for admitted patients still shows, because medians are not suppressed; ARH CTAS 1 (2 visits) shows "<5"; in the admitted-by-site matrix, KGH 31, ARH 15 and CVH 9 show, PGH shows "<5" and the total is blank, so PGH's 4 cannot be worked out by subtraction (SUP-07).

## Navigation: drillthrough, tooltips and bookmarks

- Drillthrough on DimSite[SiteCode] from any executive site visual to Site detail, keeping all filters, with a back button. RLS still applies, so a KGH user only reaches KGH.
- Tooltip page on the site bar charts: ED Visits (Shared), median minutes, % within target, LWBS Rate (Shared).
- Bookmarks: "Average daily" and "Last snapshot" swap the occupancy visuals through the Selection pane, with data off so user filters stay; "Reset filters" returns slicers to the full period.
- Page navigator on pages 1 to 3 and 6; site slicer synced on pages 2 and 3; the site bar chart filters the cards.

## Accessibility and performance

- Alt text on every visual; tab order set in the Selection pane; decorative shapes out of the tab order.
- Contrast at least 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for chart marks (Kestrel standard, based on Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 AA); data labels at least 12 pt.
- A site over target is shown by a marker and label as well as colour.
- Every visual passes "Show as a table"; titles in plain words.
- Mobile layout for Site ED operations.
- Every visual renders in 3 seconds or less in Performance Analyzer with a cleared cache (agreed).

## Approval and change log

- 1.0, 2026-10-09: pages, visuals, measures, suppression. Approved by Janelle Cardinal and Dr. Sarah Whitford.
- 1.1, 2026-10-16: drillthrough, tooltip page, bookmarks, navigation, accessibility. Same approvers.
- After go-live, changes go through the change-control board.
mistakes: Designing pages around the visuals you know instead of the questions each audience asks; a page with twenty visuals answers nothing quickly.
Listing measures without tested values, so user acceptance testing has nothing to compare against and a wrong total slips through.
Suppressing counts but showing the rate next to the visit total, or a total from which the small count can be subtracted, which lets anyone work the small count back.
Treating accessibility as colour choice only, and skipping alt text, tab order and 'Show as a table' checks that screen-reader users depend on.

items.purpose: This plan governs how the Beacon reports move from build to the people who use them: the workspaces and who holds which role, the app and its audiences, row-level security, the gateway and scheduled refresh, security settings, the deployment and change path, monitoring and rollback. Tomás Rivera (E-006) writes it with the Programme Manager, Daniel Osei (E-004) reviews the security settings, and Marcus Bell (E-002) approves it. Grace Liu (E-005) uses it to support the live service. It is written in week 5, before the first production deployment, and updated whenever a workspace, role, gateway or refresh changes.

sections.heading: Scope and principles
sections.guidance: Say which items the plan covers and the few rules everything else follows, such as app-only access, a change record for every production change, and least privilege. Good principles are short enough to remember and strict enough to settle an argument.

sections.heading: Workspaces and roles
sections.guidance: List each workspace, its purpose and who holds Admin, Member, Contributor and Viewer. Remember that row-level security filters only Viewers and app users, so every role above Viewer in production sees every site. Name end dates for supplier access. It is good when every person with a role has a reason recorded.

sections.heading: App, audiences and row-level security
sections.guidance: Describe the app, each audience, the pages it sees, the security groups that grant membership and the row-level security roles and filters. Say how the roles are tested. Good design ties every audience and role to a group in the Identity Directory (A-007), so access can be reviewed.

sections.heading: Data connection, gateway and refresh
sections.guidance: State the storage mode and why it beats the alternatives here, the gateway set-up and owner, the data source credentials and privacy level, the refresh schedule and the failure alert. A good refresh plan names the upstream job it waits for and the time data must be ready.

sections.heading: Security and sharing settings
sections.guidance: Record the sensitivity label, export settings, sharing and Build permission, endorsement and how activity is monitored. Each setting should match a security acceptance criterion so it can be tested at go-live.

sections.heading: Deployment and change path
sections.guidance: Write the numbered steps from Dev to Test to Prod: version control, deployment pipeline and rules, release checks, change approval, release window and smoke test. It is good when a second person could deploy by following the steps alone.

sections.heading: Monitoring
sections.guidance: For each thing you watch (refresh, gateway, usage, access and exports) give the check, who does it, how often, the threshold and the action. A threshold without an action is just a number on a screen.

sections.heading: Rollback
sections.guidance: List the triggers, the steps to restore the last approved version, who decides and how fast. Privacy triggers need their own path: unpublish first, then tell the Chief Privacy Officer, who decides whether breach duties apply.

| Field | Value |

| Document ID | BCN-R1-25 |
| Title | Workspace, refresh and deployment plan |
| Owner | Tomás Rivera (E-006), with the Programme Manager |
| Security review | Daniel Osei (E-004) |
| Approver | Marcus Bell (E-002) |
| Version and date | 1.0, 2026-10-14 |
| Status | Approved |

## Scope and principles

Covers the Beacon semantic model, reports and app in the Power BI service (A-009), fed from de-identified views in the Clinical Data Warehouse (A-010).

- Consumers use the app only. Nobody shares reports directly.
- Every production change has a change record.
- Least privilege: workspace roles above Viewer bypass row-level security (RLS), so production holds as few as possible.

## Workspaces and roles

| Workspace | Purpose | Admin | Contributor | Viewer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Beacon Dev | Build and unit tests on test views | Tomás Rivera | Mei Tanaka (E-013); Lumen Analytics Partners (V-05) consultants until 2026-11-30 | None |
| Beacon Test | Release checks and user acceptance testing | Tomás Rivera | None | Janelle Cardinal (E-008), Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007), Aisha Mahmoud (E-010) |
| Beacon Prod | Live service; publishes the app | Tomás Rivera; second admin pending | None | None: consumers use the app |

- No Member roles in any Beacon workspace.
- Second Prod admin: needed for R-06, but an admin sees every site, so it stays pending until a second builder is named (before Lumen leaves on 2026-11-30) and Janelle Cardinal approves all-site access for that person.
- Mei Tanaka is a Contributor in Beacon Dev only, where she works on de-identified test views. In Beacon Prod she uses the app as a Viewer in the Site CVH role, so RLS applies and an all-sites view is refused. Her excess "view all sites" grant on A-009 has been removed (SAC-06; RLS-12).
- Lumen's Contributor role is removed on 2026-11-30, when their contract ends (R-07).

## App, audiences and row-level security

- App "Beacon Patient Flow", published from Beacon Prod.
- Audience Executive: all pages; group BCN-App-Executive in the Identity Directory (A-007).
- Audience Site operations: every page except Executive overview; groups BCN-App-Site-KGH, -ARH, -CVH and -PGH.
- RLS roles on DimSite, as tested in the RLS test pack (BCN-R1-21): one role per site with the filter below (KGH shown), members from groups BCN-RLS-KGH, -ARH, -CVH and -PGH, plus All sites with the filter TRUE () for BCN-RLS-ALL. Audiences decide which pages people see; RLS decides which rows.

```
[SiteCode] = "KGH"
```

- Tests: "View as" each role in Power BI Desktop, then sign in with a real Viewer account in Beacon Test for positive and negative tests.

## Data connection, gateway and refresh

- Storage mode Import: data changes daily, volumes are small, visuals are fastest. DirectQuery would send every click through the gateway to A-010. Direct Lake needs data in OneLake, and A-010 is on premises.
- On-premises data gateway in standard mode, a two-server cluster run by Ahmed Haddad (E-017). Outbound connections only; the firewall rule is a normal change.
- Data source: service account svc-bcn-refresh, read-only on the de-identified views, no access to Restricted tables; privacy level Organizational. The credentials are encrypted and held in the gateway cloud service, and only the gateway on premises can decrypt them.
- Scheduled refresh: 05:00 Mountain Time daily, after the nightly warehouse load, which must finish before 05:00 (proposed). Dashboards then show yesterday's data by 06:00 (service level). A refresh failure alerts the service desk (Analytics Support) within 1 hour; the notification also goes to the semantic model owner.

## Security and sharing settings

- Sensitivity label Confidential on the semantic model and reports; the app shows their labels. Exports to Excel, PDF and PowerPoint carry the label; a .csv export does not, so .csv export is turned off (SAC-10) and the knowledge article tells users to export to Excel.
- Visuals export summarized data only; underlying data export is off. Publish to web is off, and reports are never shared directly: access comes only through the app.
- Build permission: Tomás Rivera and Mei Tanaka only, so consumers cannot build their own reports or analyze the model in Excel.
- The semantic model is Certified by the data steward, so analysts reuse it instead of copying extracts.
- Sam Okafor (E-020) checks the Power BI activity log monthly for exports, sharing and role changes.

## Deployment and change path

1. Build in Beacon Dev; save the Power BI project (PBIP) files to the Beacon repository with a version number.
2. Deploy to Beacon Test with the deployment pipeline. Dev uses the test views; a deployment rule points Test and Prod at the live de-identified views, so release checks run against the approved figures.
3. Run release checks: every measure's expected value from the DAX catalogue (BCN-R1-20), RLS positive and negative tests, suppression tests, accessibility and Performance Analyzer.
4. Raise a normal change in the IT Service Management Platform (A-011), approved by Marcus Bell or his delegate.
5. Deploy to Beacon Prod in the Tuesday 18:00 to 19:00 window (proposed) and update the app.
6. Smoke test: open each page as one site role and as Executive; compare five headline values with the test results.

## Monitoring

| What | Check and who | Threshold and action |
|---|---|---|
| Refresh | Failure alert within 1 hour of the 05:00 refresh; refresh history checked by 06:00 daily, Analytics Support | One failure: P3 incident. Two in a row: P2, tell Janelle Cardinal |
| Gateway | Status and server health, Ahmed Haddad | A member offline: restore the same business day |
| Usage | Usage metrics monthly, Tomás Rivera | A page unused for a month goes to the service review |
| Access and exports | Activity log monthly, Sam Okafor | Unexpected export or role change: security incident |

## Rollback

- Triggers: a release check fails in Prod; a user sees another site's rows; a count under 5 appears; two refresh failures in a row caused by the release.
- Steps: deploy the previous approved PBIP version to Test, smoke test, deploy to Prod, update the app, record it in the change.
- Privacy triggers: unpublish the app first, then roll back, and tell Priya Raman (E-003), who decides whether the Health Information Act breach duty (section 60.1, risk of harm) applies.
- Decision owner: Tomás Rivera, with Grace Liu (E-005) informed. Target: last approved version restored within 2 hours (proposed).
mistakes: Giving testers or analysts Member or Contributor roles in production: those roles bypass row-level security, so they see every site.
Sharing reports directly instead of through the app with audiences tied to security groups, which leaves access nobody can review.
Scheduling refresh before the warehouse load finishes, or with no failure alert, so leaders read stale numbers without knowing it.
Having no tested rollback, so when a release breaks a measure or a privacy control the wrong numbers stay live while the team improvises.

items.purpose: The readiness record lets the sponsor decide go-live on evidence rather than optimism, and proves the service desk has accepted a supported service. items.purpose: The lessons-learned register records what Release 1 taught the programme while it is fresh. Each lesson is an evidence-based statement with its effect, what to do differently, an owner and the place it will be applied. The Programme Manager runs a short session with the Release 1 team and keeps the register; the executive sponsor reviews it, and every Release 2 and Release 3 plan must show how its lessons were used. You open it in week 6 when Release 1 closes, add to it at every release close, and use it again at programme closure.

sections.heading: Scope and method
sections.guidance: Say which period and work the register covers, who took part and the rules for a good lesson: evidence, effect, action, owner, and no blame. A clear method stops the session turning into a list of complaints.

sections.heading: Release 1 at close
sections.guidance: Give the facts the lessons rest on: earned value at the last status date, work packages behind plan, the go-live decision and key data figures. Lessons that cite numbers are hard to argue with and easy to check later.

sections.heading: What worked
sections.guidance: Record the practices to keep, each with the evidence that it worked. Good practice is a lesson too, and it is the easiest one to repeat in the next release.

sections.heading: What to change
sections.guidance: For each lesson write what happened with evidence, the effect on the programme, what to do differently and who owns it. Describe the process or system that allowed the problem, not the person involved. A lesson nobody owns will not change anything.

sections.heading: Where each lesson is applied
sections.guidance: Link every lesson to the document, plan or register where it will be used, and say how you will know it was applied. This is what turns a register into knowledge transfer instead of an archive.

sections.heading: Review and sign-off
sections.guidance: Record who reviewed the register and when it will be reviewed again. Keep closed lessons in the register with their outcome, so the programme closure report can show what changed.

items.purpose: The continual-improvement register is where improvements to the analytics service are recorded, prioritized, owned and checked after go-live. Each entry states where it came from, the current value from data, the target, the owner, the due date, its priority score and the measure that proves the result. Grace Liu (E-005) owns it as service owner, Janelle Cardinal (E-008) agrees the priorities as business owner, and the monthly service review reads it. You create it in week 6 from the lessons-learned register, the go-live handover and the service levels, and it lives as long as the service.

sections.heading: Improvement approach
sections.guidance: Show the improvement model the register follows. Use the seven continual-improvement questions from ITIL 4, which Version 5 refines, and say where in the register each one is answered. Good registers make the vision and the baseline explicit before any action.

sections.heading: How items are prioritized
sections.guidance: Give a simple scoring rule based on value, risk reduced and effort, say who agreed the scores and what happens to low scores. A visible rule stops the loudest request jumping the queue.

sections.heading: Register
sections.guidance: One row per improvement: ID, the improvement and its source, the current value from data, the target labelled agreed or proposed, the owner and due date, and the score. Every item needs a baseline and a target, or you can never say it worked.

sections.heading: Measures and review dates
sections.guidance: For each item, name the measure, where it comes from and when it is reviewed. An item closes when the measure shows the target was reached, not when the action is done.

sections.heading: Parked and rejected ideas
sections.guidance: Record ideas not taken forward and why, so they are not raised again without new facts. Send anything that changes scope, cost or data handling to change control rather than the register.

sections.heading: Governance
sections.guidance: Say how ideas are raised, who logs and scores them, how the monthly review checks them, and the rule for closing an item. Good governance keeps the register moving instead of growing.

## Improvement approach

Each item follows the continual-improvement questions from ITIL 4, which ITIL Version 5 refines:

1. What is the vision? One trusted set of patient-flow numbers each morning, and access on the day it is needed.
2. Where are we now? The "Now" column, from data.
3. Where do we want to be? The "Target" column, agreed or proposed.
4. How do we get there? The improvement.
5. Take action: owner and due date.
6. Did we get there? The measure at the review date.
7. How do we keep the momentum going? Results go to the monthly service review, and finished items stay in the register with their result.

## How items are prioritized

Score = (value to consumers + risk reduced) ÷ effort, each rated 1 to 5 by the team. Scores are estimates agreed with Janelle Cardinal on 2026-10-27. Highest score first. Items under 3 wait until capacity frees up.

## Register

| CI-01 | Faster access to the app (LL-09) | Power BI access requests: median 4.40 days; 1 of 6 within 72 hours | 80% within 72 hours (agreed, charter) | Grace Liu, through the Release 2 value stream, 2026-11-26 | (5+4)÷2 = 4.5 |
| CI-04 | Correct emergency data at source (R-01) | 4 of 478 unique third-quarter rows quarantined; 2 more with impossible times | No quarantined rows in a month (proposed) | Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007), 2026-12-04 | (4+4)÷2 = 4.0 |
| CI-05 | Second model builder and knowledge transfer from Lumen (R-06, R-07, LL-10) | 1 person can publish a model fix | 2 people before 2026-11-30 (proposed) | Programme Manager, 2026-11-27 | (3+5)÷2 = 4.0 |
| CI-07 | Closure survey on every analytics ticket, with follow-up on low scores | Satisfaction 3.0 from 9 responses | 4.0 of 5 (proposed) | Grace Liu, 2026-11-25 | (3+1)÷1 = 4.0 |
| CI-02 | Triage guide and knowledge articles for the top incident causes | 66.7% of analytics incidents within target (8 of 12) | 90% (agreed) | Mei Tanaka (E-013), 2026-11-20 | (4+3)÷2 = 3.5 |
| CI-03 | Templates and a weekly slot for service requests | 50.0% within target (4 of 8) | 85% (agreed) | Mei Tanaka, after CI-02 | (3+2)÷2 = 2.5 |

## Measures and review dates

|---|---|---|---|

| CI-05 | People able to publish a model fix | Release log | 2026-11-25 |

- Patient-level lists on dashboards: not an improvement item. Any such request goes to the change-control board, because the Health Information Act requires the least amount of information and the highest degree of anonymity.
- CI-03 waits until CI-02 is done.

## Governance

- Anyone can raise an idea through the service desk or at the monthly service review. Grace Liu logs and scores it with Janelle Cardinal.

## Scope and sources

- Systems: Clinical Information System (CIS, A-001), Virtual Desktop Service (A-008), Bed Management System (A-006) and Beacon dashboards (A-009), all controlled through the Identity Directory (A-007).
- Events: joiner, mover, leaver and one-off requests for employees, agency nurses from ClearPath Staffing (V-03) and vendor engineers.

## How access is granted today

| Step | Who | What happens | Evidence (data) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Unit manager | Asks by phone, portal or walk-up | Phone 26, portal 16, walk-up 7 of 49 requests |
| 2 | Service desk | Logs a ticket in the IT Service Management Platform (A-011) and passes it on | All 49 assigned to Identity and Access |

| 6 | Service desk | Closes the ticket without checking access works | 3 of 49 requests reopened |

## How access is changed and removed today

- Leavers: HR records the end in the HR and Payroll System (A-015), but no event reaches IT. Access goes only if a manager raises a ticket.
- Agency nurses: contract end dates stay with ClearPath Staffing; nobody tells Kestrel.

Neither missed leaver signed in to the directory after their end date (E-027 last 2026-08-13, E-014 last 2026-08-29); CIS audit logs still need checking.

## Causes across the four dimensions

- Organizations and People: one administrator approves, provisions and runs audit logs; managers do not see access decisions as theirs.
- Information and Technology: no HR feed into A-007; tickets store only opened and resolved times.
- Partners and Suppliers: ClearPath and Meridian need not tell Kestrel when a worker ends; ClearPath has no assurance report on file.
- Value Streams and Processes: approval, checks and provisioning run one after another by phone and email; permissions go one by one, not as a role.

## Baseline and immediate actions

| Measure | Baseline (data) | Target (agreed) |
|---|---|---|
| Access requests resolved within 72 hours | 27.3% | 80% |
| Median days to fulfil an access request | 4.26 | 1 |
| Missed leavers | 2 | 0 |
| Privileged accounts with MFA | 66.7% | 100% |
| Q3 access reviews completed on time | 66.7% | 100% |

1. Disable E-014 and E-027 today, remove their permissions, check CIS activity after their end dates (I-02). Owner: Daniel Osei.
2. Remove approve access and administer audit logs from E-009; re-approve his rights through E-004 (I-01). Owner: Daniel Osei.
3. Remove E-028's old Unit Clerk permissions. Owner: Grace Liu.
4. Enrol E-009 and E-015 in MFA; end-date E-015 no later than the Meridian contract end. Owner: Daniel Osei.
5. Escalate the 6 overdue reviews to each reviewer's manager. Owner: Grace Liu.
mistakes: Drawing the process as policy says it works instead of as the data shows it works.
Measuring only the request queue and missing removal; the missed leavers and the mover's old access are the biggest risks.
Blaming the administrator instead of the design that gives one person approve, provision and audit-log rights.
Waiting for the future-state design before disabling accounts that should already be gone.

sections.heading: Scope and basis

sections.heading: Duration estimates and schedule risk

sections.heading: Baseline status and approval

items.purpose: The procurement and vendor-risk plan decides what Release 2 buys and how (make or buy, contract type, supplier selection), and which security, privacy and access controls every supplier must accept, especially for the identity platform and for agency and vendor workers who hold Kestrel accounts. The Programme Manager writes it with Daniel Osei (E-004) and Priya Raman (E-003). Marcus Bell (E-002) approves it and awards contracts within budget; each contract has a named owner. It is used from week 7 until every contract closes, and its supplier controls stay in force after Beacon ends.

sections.heading: Procurement needs
sections.guidance: List each thing Release 2 must obtain from outside, the work package that funds it and the evidence that it is needed. Needs should come from the baseline and the current-state findings, not from a product someone likes.

sections.heading: Make-or-buy decisions
sections.guidance: For each need say make, buy or amend an existing contract, and why: skills, time, cost, control. Good decisions keep in-house the work that depends on Kestrel's own knowledge.

sections.heading: Contract approach
sections.guidance: Choose the contract type for each item and explain the choice by where the scope uncertainty sits. Fixed price suits clear scope; time and materials with a cap suits uncertain scope. Add holdbacks or acceptance terms that protect the buyer.

sections.heading: Supplier selection
sections.guidance: Set mandatory pass or fail criteria first, then weighted scoring criteria that add to 100%, and say who agreed them and how suppliers are invited. Criteria must reflect clinical needs and security, not price alone.

sections.heading: Supplier risk and access controls
sections.guidance: For each existing supplier give the findings from data, the controls required and an owner. Treat supplier workers as identities with a start, an end and reviews. Good controls name the contract clause or account change that makes them real.

sections.heading: Privacy and data location
sections.guidance: Say which law applies to the information the suppliers handle, what Alberta law does and does not require, and which requirements are Kestrel policy or contract terms. Do not present a contract rule as law.

sections.heading: Procurement schedule and budget
sections.guidance: Give dated steps from approved statement of work to contract award and start of work, tied to the task that needs the supplier. Show the budget source for each contract and the rule for going over it.

sections.heading: Contract management and closure
sections.guidance: Name contract owners, how performance is reviewed, how contract changes are controlled and what closure requires: acceptance, holdback release, access removal and lessons. Closure is where supplier access is most often forgotten.

## Make-or-buy decisions

- PR-1: buy. Kestrel has no MFA skills in-house and task 15 starts 2026-10-26. The role catalogue, approval rules and value stream stay in-house (make), because they depend on Kestrel's roles.
- PR-2: buy as a change order under NorthArc's existing contract, because only NorthArc can change the hosted system's outbound feed.

## Contract approach

| Item | Contract type | Why |
|---|---|---|
| PR-1 subscription | Fixed price per user per year, 3-year term with exit and data-return terms (proposed) | Predictable cost, clean exit |
| PR-1 implementation | Firm fixed price against a statement of work (SOW) with acceptance criteria; 10% held back until the Release 2 gate | Scope is clear (four sites, shared workstations, pilot); the seller carries cost risk |
| PR-2 HR feed | Time and materials with a not-to-exceed cap | Scope stays uncertain until HR data errors (E-028 overlap, E-037 unknown manager) are understood |
| PR-3, PR-4 | Amendments | Terms change, price does not |

## Supplier selection

Mandatory, pass or fail:
- Kestrel data held in Canada (a Kestrel contract requirement).
- An independent assurance report under 12 months old: System and Organization Controls (SOC) 2 Type II or equivalent.
- Breach notice to Kestrel within 24 hours (proposed); right to audit; MFA on the supplier's own administrator access.

Scored (agreed by Marcus Bell, Daniel Osei and Janelle Cardinal, E-008): sign-in speed at shared clinical workstations (R-03) 30%; security and assurance 25%; fit with the Identity Directory (A-007) and Virtual Desktop Service (A-008) 20%; three-year cost 15%; ability to start on 2026-10-26 10%. Only suppliers already on Kestrel's approved list are invited, so award can happen by 2026-10-22.

## Supplier risk and access controls

| Supplier | Finding (data, 2026-10-01) | Control required | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| V-01 Meridian | Remote access; E-015 privileged, no MFA, no end date, extra chart permission; assurance 2026-03-31 | Named accounts; MFA before the next session; end date no later than contract end (2029-03-31); remove chart permission; each session approved | Daniel Osei |
| V-02 NorthArc | Remote access; E-039 privileged with MFA, ends 2026-12-31, kept under an exception (AR-010); assurance 2026-05-15 | Exception expiry date; monitored sessions; HR feed change order | Daniel Osei |
| V-03 ClearPath | No assurance report on file; E-014 enabled 31 days after contract end; agency and vendor awareness training 48% | Tell Kestrel HR of every start, change and end within 1 business day (proposed); training before an account; assurance report or Kestrel questionnaire by 2026-12-31 | Nora Lindqvist (E-018) |
| V-05 Lumen | Remote access; assurance 2025-06-30, over 12 months old; contract ends 2026-11-30 | Remove all access on 2026-11-30; knowledge transfer first (R-07) | Programme Manager |

## Privacy and data location

- The identity platform holds staff personal information: names, roles, sign-in logs. Staff records fall under the Protection of Privacy Act; patient health information stays under the Health Information Act.
- No Alberta statute bans storing this information outside Canada. "Data in Canada" is a Kestrel contract requirement, so PR-1 makes it a mandatory criterion.
- Sign-in logs are not sent to Sentinel SOC Services (V-04), which processes data in the United States, until Priya Raman closes the privacy review and contract safeguards under R-05.

|---|---|
| 2026-10-09 | SOW and selection criteria approved |
| 2026-10-14 | Responses due |
| 2026-10-16 | Evaluation panel scores responses |
| 2026-10-22 | Contract award by Marcus Bell |

Budget (estimates from the Release 2 cost baseline): PR-1 first-year subscription CAD 38,000 and implementation CAD 42,000, inside WP-108's CAD 130,000; PR-2 capped at CAD 30,000 inside WP-107's CAD 110,000. Anything above these needs a change request.

## Contract management and closure

- Contract owners: PR-1 the WP-108 owner; PR-2 and PR-3 Nora Lindqvist; PR-4 Daniel Osei.
- Monthly review of each supplier against SOW milestones and the access controls above.
- Contract changes go through Beacon change control before any amendment is signed.
- Closure: acceptance against the SOW at the Release 2 gate releases the holdback; supplier accounts and remote access are removed or end-dated; lessons go to the lessons-learned register.
mistakes: Choosing fixed price for work whose scope is still unknown, then paying for it through a stream of change orders.
Checking a supplier's security once at signing and never again; assurance reports age and access piles up.
Forgetting that supplier workers are identities: agency and vendor accounts need a start, an end and reviews like employees.
Writing 'the law requires data to stay in Canada': it is a Kestrel contract requirement, and the Health Information Act requires safeguards, not a location.

items.purpose: This plan prepares clinicians, managers, agency and vendor workers and the service desk for multifactor authentication, single sign-on and the new access-request route, and measures whether they adopt them. It covers who is affected and how much, the readiness approach, the messages and channels, training and support, resistance and risks, and adoption measures with targets. The Programme Manager writes it with Janelle Cardinal (E-008), who owns the risk that MFA slows clinicians (R-03), Grace Liu (E-005) and Nora Lindqvist (E-018). Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001) sends the key messages and approves it. It runs from week 7 through the Release 2 gate and the first month after.

sections.heading: Change summary and goals
sections.guidance: Say in plain words what changes for people, when, and which tasks deliver it, then give the goal in one sentence. A clinician reading it should know what will be different on their next shift.

sections.heading: Who is affected
sections.guidance: List each group, its size or evidence from data, what changes for it and the impact level. Use the data to find who carries the change; here every enabled clinical account lacks MFA, so clinicians carry most of it.

sections.heading: Readiness approach (ADKAR)
sections.guidance: Plan each stage of awareness, desire, knowledge, ability and reinforcement with a concrete action and owner. Good plans give people a reason before they give them a training course.

sections.heading: Communication schedule
sections.guidance: Give dated messages by audience, with the content, channel and sender. The sponsor explains why, managers explain what it means locally, and the service desk hears everything before users do.

sections.heading: Training and support
sections.guidance: Describe the training, where and when help is available, super users and how agency and vendor workers are reached. Cover nights and weekends, because clinical work does not stop at 17:00.

sections.heading: Resistance and risks
sections.guidance: Name each likely objection or risk, its owner and the response. Treat a concern such as slower sign-in as something to measure, not something to argue away.

sections.heading: Adoption measures
sections.guidance: List measures of adoption, not attendance, with the baseline from data, the target labelled agreed or proposed, and how often they are checked. Good measures show whether the new way of working actually took hold.

## Change summary and goals

- Clinicians enrol in multifactor authentication (MFA) and use single sign-on (SSO) at shared workstations: task 15, 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-06.
- Access starts and ends from human resources (HR) events: task 14, to 2026-11-10.

Sign-in time on Medicine 4A is timed before the change, and Janelle Cardinal decides go or no-go from the pilot data.
- Release 2 pilot of the whole access service (request form, HR-driven access, MFA and SSO) on KGH Medicine 4A and the KGH emergency department: task 19, 2026-11-23 to 2026-11-26.

Goal: clinicians keep working at the speed of care while every account becomes provable.

## Who is affected

| Group | Evidence (data, 2026-10-01) | What changes | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nurses, physicians, unit clerks, agency nurses | 19 enabled accounts, 0 enrolled in MFA | Enrol MFA; new sign-in at shared workstations | High |
| Agency nurses (ClearPath Staffing, V-03) | 2 of the 19; awareness training for agency and vendor workers 48% | Enrol and train on the first shift; access ends with the contract | High |
| Managers and charge nurses | Reviewers for 24 third-quarter review items | Request by form; HR start dates drive access; quarterly attestation | Medium |
| Vendor support (V-01, V-02) | 2 accounts, 1 enrolled | MFA on every session; named accounts only | Medium |
| Service desk | 3 analysts | New knowledge articles; enrolment help | Medium |

## Readiness approach (ADKAR)

ADKAR: awareness, desire, knowledge, ability, reinforcement. Each stage gets an action and an owner.

| Stage | Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Awareness | Sponsor message on why: two missed leavers, four-day waits for access, the board's question about cyber risk | Dr. Helen Marchetti |
| Desire | Show the gain: one sign-in, and access ready on the first shift | Janelle Cardinal |
| Knowledge | 10-minute e-learning, quick reference card, huddle talks | Grace Liu |
| Ability | Enrolment desks at each site; super users on every shift in the first week | Site nurse leads |
| Reinforcement | Weekly enrolment results by site, fixes from feedback, thanks from the sponsor | Programme Manager |

## Communication schedule

| Date | Audience | Message | Channel and sender |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-19 | All clinical staff | Why, what and when | Email and unit huddles; Dr. Helen Marchetti |
| 2026-10-20 | Managers and charge nurses | Your role: start dates, the request form, attestation | 30-minute briefing; Nora Lindqvist and Grace Liu |
| 2026-10-21 | ClearPath, Meridian Clinical Systems (V-01), NorthArc Cloud (V-02) | MFA on every account, end dates, training before access | Contract letter; Daniel Osei (E-004) |
| 2026-10-22 | Service desk | Scripts, knowledge articles, escalation | Briefing; Grace Liu |
| 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-06 | Clinical staff by site | Your enrolment slot and where to get help | Huddles and workstation posters; super users |
| Weekly from 2026-10-30 | Leaders | Enrolment by site, issues and fixes | Status email; Programme Manager |
| 2026-11-20 | Pilot units | The new request route starts 2026-11-23 | Huddle; Janelle Cardinal |
| 2026-11-27 | All staff | Results and next steps | Email; Dr. Helen Marchetti |

## Training and support

- E-learning: 10 minutes, completed before enrolment and recorded in training records.
- Enrolment desks: one per site, day and evening shifts, 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-06.
- Super users: Aisha Mahmoud (E-010) for the KGH emergency department and Ben Kowalski (E-011) for KGH Medicine 4A; one more per site, named by the site nurse lead.
- Night staff: super users on night shifts in the first week; a desk phone line for enrolment problems.
- Agency nurses: enrol and finish awareness training on the first shift, before access to the Clinical Information System (the ClearPath amendment requires it).
- Service desk: knowledge articles for enrolment, lost device and sign-in failure; escalation to Identity and Access.

## Resistance and risks

- R-03, owner Janelle Cardinal: MFA prompts slow clinicians at shared workstations. Response: time sign-in on Medicine 4A before the change, then again in the Medicine 4A pilot inside task 15, before any other unit changes; the MFA and SSO recommendation sets how often prompts appear; Janelle Cardinal stops the rollout to other units if sign-in time rises.
- "One more password": SSO removes separate sign-ins, so show the count of sign-ins before and after.
- Physicians have the lowest awareness training completion of any employee group (71%): Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007) briefs physicians herself.
- Night and weekend staff miss briefings: evening desk hours and night super users.

## Adoption measures

| Measure | Baseline (data) | Target | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enabled clinical accounts enrolled in MFA | 0 of 19 | 95% by 2026-11-06, 100% by 2026-11-26 (proposed) | Weekly |
| Privileged accounts with MFA | 66.7% | 100% (agreed) | Weekly |
| Security awareness, agency and vendor workers | 48% | 90% (agreed) | Monthly |
| Access requests through the portal form | 16 of 49 (32.7%) | 90% (proposed) | Monthly |
| Password reset tickets | 27 in August and September | Half that rate after SSO (proposed) | Monthly |
| Sign-in time at shared workstations | Timed on KGH Medicine 4A before the change | No increase (agreed with Janelle Cardinal); 10 seconds or less from badge tap to open chart (proposed) | Medicine 4A pilot in task 15, then weekly |
| Clinician satisfaction with the change | Pilot survey | 4 of 5 (proposed) | 2026-11-27 |
mistakes: Sending one launch email and calling it change management; people need a reason, skills, help and reinforcement as well as the news.
Measuring training attendance instead of adoption; enrolment, use of the new form and fewer password resets show whether the change took hold.
Planning for day shifts only, so night and agency staff meet MFA for the first time at 03:00 with nobody to help.
Dismissing the sign-in speed concern instead of measuring it in the pilot and acting on the result.

items.purpose: The value stream document maps how a clinician's access request flows from trigger to working access across the ITIL Version 5 lifecycle stages, measures work and wait time at each step, and designs a future state that removes the waits. Grace Liu (E-005) owns the access service and the document, the Programme Manager facilitates, and Nora Lindqvist (E-018), Daniel Osei (E-004) and Priya Raman (E-003) review it. sections.heading: Service, consumers and outcome

## Service, consumers and outcome

- Service: access to the Clinical Information System (CIS, A-001), Virtual Desktop Service (A-008) and Beacon dashboards (A-009) for joiners, movers, leavers and one-off requests.
- Consumers: clinicians, agency nurses (ClearPath Staffing, V-03), vendor engineers (Meridian Clinical Systems, V-01) and their managers.
- Outcome: the right access on the first shift, and none after the last.
- Utility: working, role-correct access. Warranty: ready at shift start, protected by multifactor authentication (MFA) and least privilege, provable.

## Baseline from the service desk data

Access requests in khn_service_desk.csv, 2026-08-01 to 2026-09-30, before Release 2; duplicate removed, flags recomputed.

- 49 logged, 44 resolved, 3 reopened.
- Median lead time 102.3 hours (4.26 days); middle half 70.1 to 154.5 hours (quartiles by the exclusive method, as PERCENTILE.EXC returns them).
- 27.3% resolved within 72 hours; 15.2% met the service-level target.

## Lifecycle map

| Stage | Meaning for the access service | Owner | Measure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discover | 5 to 6 requests a week, Monday peaks, 4-day waits, 2 missed leavers | Grace Liu | This baseline |
| Design | Role bundles, pre-approval and segregation-of-duties rules, one form | Daniel Osei | Role matrix |
| Acquire | Human resources (HR) feed (NorthArc Cloud, V-02), ClearPath end dates, MFA platform | Programme Manager | Procurement plan |
| Build | Ticket workflow, HR link to the Identity Directory (A-007), knowledge articles | Kevin Park (E-009) | Configured workflow |
| Transition | Pilot on Kestrel General Hospital (KGH) Medicine 4A and KGH emergency, training, change approval | Grace Liu | Pilot results |
| Operate | Directory, HR feed and provisioning jobs run daily | Kevin Park | Feed failures |
| Deliver | Each request fulfilled | Grace Liu | Lead time |
| Support | Sign-in faults, password resets, reopened requests | Grace Liu | Reopen rate |

## Current-state value stream

| Step | Stage | Who | Work (h) | Wait (h) | Complete and accurate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Manager asks by phone, portal or walk-up | Deliver | Manager | 0.25 | 0 | 60% |
| 2 Desk logs and routes | Deliver | Desk | 0.25 | 3.0 | 100% |
| 3 Desk confirms with the manager (no HR check) | Deliver | Desk | 0.25 | 7.0 | 90% |
| 4 Approve access | Deliver | Kevin Park | 0.10 | 18.0 | 95% |
| 5 Check CIS training | Deliver | Educator | 0.10 | 6.0 | 100% |
| 6 Provision account and permissions | Deliver, Operate | Kevin Park | 1.00 | 57.0 | 85% |
| 7 Issue credentials | Deliver | Desk | 0.25 | 4.0 | 100% |
| 8 Clinician signs in and tests | Deliver | Clinician | 0.25 | 3.0 | 93% |
| 9 Close ticket | Deliver | Desk | 0.10 | 1.75 | 100% |
| Total | | | 2.55 | 99.75 | 40.6% rolled |

Flow efficiency = 2.55 ÷ 102.3 = 2.5%: the request waits 97.5% of the time.

## How the times were derived

1. Lead time (data): resolved_at minus opened_at; median 102.3 hours, n = 44.
2. Tickets hold only two timestamps, so step times are not in the data. Work times are estimates from a timed walk-through on 2026-11-12 of five requests near the median: SD-10154, SD-10060, SD-10004, SD-10166, SD-10045.
3. Total wait = 102.3 minus 2.55 = 99.75 hours, split by the walk-through and checked against khn_user_permissions.csv (20 clinical workers: first permission a median 1.5 days after start; the role's permissions spread over a median 3 separate days).
4. Step 8's 93% is data (41 of 44 not reopened); other percentages are estimates.

## Four dimensions and guiding principles

- Organizations and People: one administrator approves and provisions (I-01).
- Information and Technology: no HR feed; two timestamps a ticket.
- Partners and Suppliers: ClearPath and Meridian do not report starts and ends.
- Value Streams and Processes: one-at-a-time permissions cause the longest wait.
- Principles: Focus on value (access ready for the first shift); Keep it simple and practical (no approval for standard bundles); Progress iteratively with feedback (pilot first); Optimize and automate (only after simplifying).

## Future-state value stream

| Step | Stage | Who | Work (h, estimate) | Wait (h, target) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 HR records hire or move, start date, role | Deliver | HR | 0.25 | 0 |
| 2 HR event raises the request; standard bundle pre-approved | Operate | Automated | 0 | 1.0 |
| 3 Owner approves non-standard access only | Deliver | Business owner | 0.10 | 4.0 |
| 4 Provision the whole bundle at once | Operate | Identity and Access | 0.25 | 8.0 |
| 5 MFA and training at orientation | Deliver | Desk, educator | 0.25 | 8.0 |
| 6 Sign-in on the first shift, confirmed | Deliver | Clinician, desk | 0.25 | 2.0 |
| Total | | | 1.10 | 23.0 |

Lead time about 24 hours, matching the agreed 1-day median (flow efficiency about 4.6%). The clock starts at the HR event, before the start date, so access is ready on the first shift. Leavers are disabled on their HR end date; movers lose the old bundle when the new one is granted.

## Improvement actions and measures

| Action | Owner | Due | Measure, baseline to target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-approved role bundles | Daniel Osei | 2026-11-20 | Requests needing manual approval |
| HR events drive requests and removals | Nora Lindqvist | 2026-11-20 | Missed leavers 2 to 0 (agreed) |
| One portal form | Grace Liu | 2026-11-23 | Portal share 16 of 49 to 90% (proposed) |
| Step timestamps in tickets | Grace Liu | 2026-11-23 | Steps measured from data: 0 of 9 to all |
| Pilot on two KGH units | Grace Liu | 2026-11-26 | In 72 hours 27.3% to 80%; median days 4.26 to 1 (agreed) |

Re-measured from data after one pilot month.
mistakes: Placing steps in lifecycle stages without measuring them, which gives a picture but no improvement target.
Presenting walk-through estimates as data; say which times come from timestamps and which from people.
Automating the current steps as they are, which makes a bad flow faster instead of removing its waits.
Mapping joiners only and forgetting that leavers and movers run through the same stream with higher risk.
